title: The Magnolia band and rehearsals as parties
summary: Foster joins the Magnolia band and describes rehearsals with food, dancing and the police permit.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Roy played guitar, see. Roy was our trumpet player for a long time then. Roy got on trombone. And we played, we played little things. The biggest thing we played when we had our band was that they'd lose that to drive and the funk back it. And then I got acquainted with Louis Kepertner, Eddie Gauldin's brother, which is a trombone player, Johnny Gauldin, he played violin and a little hurry up trombone, we called it hurry up trombone, see. When he couldn't play he looked like he was in a hurry to make his notes. Johnny had a job and Eddie had to go off with the order band this night, so he said, Eddie of God sent me. And Louis Kepertner was playing, and Louis Kepertner and Dave, they had a little band down in town, but I didn't know nothing about it, see. The Magnolia band. So they asked me to play with them. This was a Saturday night, I said, would I come down and play that Sunday? I went down and play that Sunday, and then they started to rave about me playing, then we got this little band and we called rehearsal, we had rehearsal twice a week. Our rehearsal was like a party. See, band rehearsal in this room and a bunch of girls and boys dancing in that next room. That's right. See, now they didn't interfere with you rehearsing in here. They were just going and dancing. See, they going and dancing. And once in a while, here come the lemonade cake and your red beans and rice, man, it's like a dinner. See, because I know we used to go to John Vien, I was at rehearsal. Man, you go to a party, man. You're bad rehearsing, man. You serve your food, red beans and rice and barbecue. You had everything. Wine and beer. See, then you had to pay, you get 50 cents, you go down and get your permit. No, for all, I was going to pay 50 cents for it. And the cops come on, see what's always noise, but you got your permit, see, you couldn't stop yourself. And if you know the cop on the beat, you tell him to go to the rehearsal night, but it's okay, see. You didn't know that cop on the beat. See, you had to get a permit.
